references.text: God consecrated all the firstborn in Israel to Himself, which forms the basis for the Levites' role as a substitute for the firstborn.
The command to dedicate all the firstborn to the Lord, including animals, which the Levites and their livestock now replace.
Earlier in the same chapter, the principle is explained that the Levites are taken in place of all the firstborn in Israel.
Repeats the command that the Levites shall be taken in place of the firstborn, and the Levites' livestock in place of the firstborn's livestock.
Confirms that the Levites are given to the Lord as a substitute for all the firstborn in Israel.
The laws concerning the redemption of firstborn humans and animals, for which the Levites serve as a substitute.
Firstborn livestock already belong to the Lord, which explains why the Levites' livestock replace the Israelites' firstborn animals.
Refers to the assembly of the firstborn in heaven, pointing back to the special status of the firstborn in Israel.
